overall: Atlanta is running warmer than NWP model guidance on this sunny, breezy June afternoon. As of 13:05 ET the running max has already hit 82.9°F — essentially at the NWP model ceiling of 82.3–82.7°F — while the predicted peak hour is still roughly an hour away (~14:12 ET). Conditions are partly sunny (38% cloud fraction, SCT ceiling) with a northwest wind around 14 mph and a positive short-term velocity, suggesting the day is still heating.
forecast_obs_notes: NWS text, ECMWF (82.3°F), HRRR (82.7°F), and NBM (82.6°F) are in tight agreement and all point to a high near 83°F, but the observed running max of 82.9°F has already eclipsed the full-day model consensus before the peak timing window has closed. This upside surprise relative to NWP guidance — combined with a still-positive velocity (+1.8°F/hr) and acceleration (+2.7°F/hr²) — implies a modest overshoot of model forecasts is likely.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max at 82.9°F and the intraday dynamics model still projecting a peak around 14:12 ET, the high is most likely to land in the 84–85°F range; the META model assigns 32% probability to 84–85°F and its expected value centers near 85°F. NWP models appear to be slightly underforecasting today's warmth, and the trajectory supports at least another 1–2°F of heating before the afternoon winds down. Confidence is moderate — the NW winds could cap gains, but the current momentum and positive acceleration favor a final high near 84.5°F.
